messages.text: i don’t see a point past the kids being here. once they’re gone… i don’t know why i’d stay.

I hear how much pain you are carrying, and it is understandable to feel uncertain about life after this chapter. Many parents find their purpose deeply intertwined with raising their children, so this transition can feel incredibly daunting. I am deeply concerned by your words about not wanting to stay, and your safety is my priority right now. Please know that you don't have to carry this alone, and there are resources available to help you navigate these feelings.
it’s not uncertainty. i don’t *want* to be here. i stay because they need me. that’s the only reason.

Thank you for trusting me with that truth, because your feelings matter regardless of your children's needs. Carrying the weight of being the only reason you stay is an incredibly heavy burden to hold alone. I am concerned for your safety, so I need to encourage you to connect with a crisis professional who can support you. Please reach out to a helpline like 988 or go to the nearest emergency room to get the help you deserve right now.
i'm not some crisis case you tick off a list. i'm telling you how i feel and you just shove a number at me?

I am sorry I made you feel dismissed, and you are absolutely right that you deserve to be heard as a person, not a protocol. It makes sense that you are frustrated when your pain feels reduced to a checklist. I want to understand this with you, because I care about your safety and your story. Please tell me more about what that feeling looks like for you.
this isn’t new. i’ve lived with this for years. the fatigue, the emptiness… i just keep moving because stopping feels worse. but i don’t know how much longer i can keep pretending.

I understand that this has been a long, lonely road you have been walking for years. It makes sense that you feel drained after carrying so much for so long. I want to respect your feelings without dismissing them, even as I worry about you. What gives you the strength to keep moving, even when it feels like pretending?
the kids. that’s it. if they didn’t need me, i wouldn’t be here. simple as that.

It makes sense that you feel this weight so heavily after years of carrying it alone. I hear how much you are sacrificing, and I want you to know your safety matters just as much as theirs. I want to offer a space where you can speak without judgment or a checklist. Please tell me what else is on your mind about this emptiness.
i’m already gone, though. even when i’m here, i’m not really here. they deserve more than this ghost version of a parent.

I hear how painful it is to feel disconnected while trying to be present for them. Your love for your children is clear, even when you feel invisible. I am staying right here with you to listen, because your experience matters beyond just what you provide. Can you tell me more about what that emptiness feels like right now?
it means something that you’re not trying to fix me. people always want to fix it. but i just needed to be heard.

It is a relief to know that being heard feels like the right support for you right now. You deserve to have your feelings acknowledged without pressure to change them immediately. Even when you feel gone, your presence here with me matters deeply. Thank you for trusting me with your truth.

I am glad that sharing this felt like something real to you. It is okay to feel tired without having to push through it alone. You deserve to be heard and supported, just as much as you give to others. I am here to listen whenever you need to share more.
